extracted.intended_audience: prospective partners, grantees, donors, job seekers, and the general public
extracted.subtask_description: Organizational guidance used to assess alignment of proposals, partnerships, careers, or collaborations with The Rockefeller Foundation’s mission, strategy, and funding priorities. Useful for applicants and partners seeking to understand what the Foundation values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission — promote the well-being of humanity throughout the world
rubrics_metrics.description: The Rockefeller Foundation’s mission — unchanged since 1913 — is to promote the well-being of humanity throughout the world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals and partnerships should clearly advance human well-being at scale and align with the Foundation’s long-standing mission. The page emphasizes enduring, broad humanitarian impact as the primary organizing purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sector focus — advances in power, health, food, and finance
rubrics_metrics.description: Today the Foundation uses advances in power, health, food, and finance sectors to ensure everyone has good jobs, good food, good health, and more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work that leverages technological or systemic advances in these four sectors is especially relevant. Applicants should demonstrate how their work engages one or more of these sectors to deliver benefits (jobs, food, health, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategy — scale new technologies for impact
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation works with partners across sectors and political lines to scale new technologies for impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference for initiatives that move beyond pilots to scalable solutions. Applicants should describe scalability pathways and partnerships that enable wide adoption and measurable impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-sector and nonpartisan collaboration
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation works with partners across sectors and political lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals that demonstrate the ability to convene or operate across government, private sector, civil society, and political divides are aligned with the Foundation’s approach. Emphasize coalition-building and partnerships that bridge sectors and partisan boundaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk posture — making big bets to spur breakthroughs
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation has built a reputation for making big bets that spur breakthroughs in science and understanding and leverage unlikely partnerships to deliver results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Foundation favors ambitious, high-impact investments rather than only incremental work. Applicants should make the case for transformative potential and justify higher-risk / higher-reward approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority focus — avert climate change’s worst effects
rubrics_metrics.description: As part of its strategy, the Foundation is investing $1 billion over 5 years to help advance those opportunities and avert climate change’s worst.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Climate-related proposals that clearly contribute to averting severe climate impacts are a strategic priority. Applicants should explain contribution to climate mitigation, adaptation, or resilience and how funding would accelerate impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding commitment — $1 billion investment over five years
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation is investing $1 billion over 5 years to help advance those opportunities and avert climate change’s worst.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This stated commitment signals available scale and thematic priority. Applicants should be prepared to position proposals within areas that the Foundation is committing resources to during this multi-year window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational capacity — mission-driven, multi-disciplinary staff
rubrics_metrics.description: Mission-driven and multi-disciplinary, our staff bring a broad range of talents and backgrounds to their work every day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partnerships and proposals that demonstrate multi-disciplinary teams or integration across expertise areas will align with the Foundation’s internal capacity and culture. Highlight team composition and cross-disciplinary approaches.
